decision.detail: I turn away from the coffee table without looking at the piano, the driver outside the window, or the Rialto letter on the lobby desk. I unbutton my jacket, reach into the left breast pocket, and pull out the coach ticket. I hold it up to the lobby light. The number matches the number I remember. I check the face of my watch: 1:47. The coach is at 3:15. That's enough time. I walk to the coat-check, take my coat off the hook, pull it over my shoulders. The gloves are in the inside pocket. I feel them. I walk to the door. I push it open. I step onto the sidewalk. The delivery van's backfire is still echoing in the brick. I walk toward the Greyhound stop. I do not look back at the lobby. I do not turn to watch the driver jack his car. I do not go inside to sit at the piano. I walk. My shoes hit the sidewalk in a steady, unremarkable rhythm. I reach the stop. The bench is here. I sit. I put my ticket on my knee. I put my hands in my coat pockets. I close my eyes. I wait for the bus.
decision.intention: Be on the coach by 3:15. Be in the back seat, window side, by 3:30. Be asleep before we cross the bridge. Be at the Pittsburgh terminal by six. Be at her door at 7:15 with the gloves in my hand and the coffee money in my pocket and the blankets rolled under my arm. Tell the driver not to sit in the driveway. The couch is a couch. I am in Pittsburgh. That is the whole forecast.
decision.words: I say nothing to Rita. I say nothing to Larry. I nod once, past them, toward the door. That is the whole conversation.
